title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + defrag scheduling to reduce fragmentation, paging, and spillover
author: Ava Patel
description:
Context: production KV cache fragmentation and spillover events have been a persistent source of tail latency and increased GPU memory pressure for long-context workloads. This PR implements an adaptive eviction policy combined with low-impact defragmentation scheduling and spillover-aware paging heuristics. Motivation: reduce out-of-memory spillover frequency, cut background paging I/O, and lower p99 generation latency during mixed short/long context traffic. High level changes: 1) Adaptive eviction scoring that weights recency, token-count footprint, and fragmentation impact to prefer evicting small high-fragmentation segments first; 2) Opportunistic defragmentation scheduler that runs incremental compaction during low-CPU/low-GPU utilization windows and yields to critical inference workloads; 3) Spillover-aware paging: when RAM->GPU spillover is required, we now prefer coalesced page movement and prefetch predicted prefixes for warm KV entries; 4) Integration with continuous batching: batch scheduler now marks requests touching high-fragmentation KV regions to avoid batching boosts that would exacerbate eviction pressure; 5) Telemetry & defensive guards: per-device fragmentation metrics, eviction-only dry-run mode, and a circuit-breaker to disable background compaction when IO or latency regressions are detected. Implementation notes: - New eviction_strategy::{adaptive,score} modules with unit tests covering score stability under skewed workloads. - Defrag scheduler implemented in runtime/defrag_scheduler.cc with an async workqueue and backpressure hooks into the serving runtime. - Paging changes in runtime/paging_manager.{cc,h} to batch IO and add prefetch path. - Continuous batching integration required small changes to scheduler: serving/scheduler.cc (batch tagging) and tests updated in serving/scheduler_tests.cc. - Added perf microbench harness (bench/kv_eviction_bench) and a soak test for spillover scenarios. Performance summary (internal perf runs on p4d.24xlarge-like infra): - Spillover event rate reduced from 23 events/hour -> 4 events/hour under synthetic long-tail workload (-82%). - Average eviction IO bytes decreased by 35% due to coalesced paging and compaction. - p99 token generation latency improved by ~18% for long-context chat traces that previously triggered spillover. - Background compaction CPU usage is <4% of a single core when idle windows are available; scheduler preempts compaction on load spikes. Backwards compatibility and rollout: - Feature gated behind runtime flag kv_eviction_adaptive=true and defrag_scheduler=on. - Default rollout plan: start with dry-run eviction scoring (no evictions) in canary, then enable eviction-only, then enable background defrag in staged regions. - No wire or on-disk format changes. Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for eviction scoring and defrag scheduler
- [x] Integration tests for paging prefetch path
- [x] Perf harness and benchmark results recorded
- [x] Telemetry added to console (fragmentation metrics + spillover counts)
- [x] Feature flags and safe rollout plan included
Related: ENG-2345 (kv fragmentation work), ENG-2411 (continuous batching interactions).

review_comments: Diego: Can you explain the heuristics that balance size vs fragmentation score? Looks reasonable but curious about edge cases where evicting many small fragments causes prefix misses.

Author (Ava): The scoring formula multiplies normalized_fragmentation_score by log(token_count+1) to penalize very large entries; small fragments get prioritized only when fragmentation_penalty > threshold. Added tests for pathological cases.
Liam: Defrag scheduler preemption looks good but ensure preemption path is lock-free to avoid stalling hot inference threads.

Author: Defrag work runs on separate worker threads and uses atomic state + try_lock where necessary; also added a safety path to abort compaction if a latency SLO trigger is seen (see runtime/defrag_scheduler.h).
Sofia: Can we expose a metric for coalesced IO bytes? Would help detect regressions when running on NVMe-backed instances.
Author: Added fragmentation_coalesced_io_bytes and exposed it to telemetry; dashboards updated.
Maya: CI failed on first run due to a flaky scheduling test; fixed by increasing the test timeout and adding deterministic seeding for the scheduler test harness.
Diego: Approved after validating perf numbers and reviewing the feature flag gating and rollout plan.
Liam: LGTM, minor nits addressed in follow-up commit.
release_notes: Improves KV cache eviction and defragmentation: reduces spillover events, lowers eviction IO, and improves p99 latency for long-context workloads. Feature gated; enable via kv_eviction_adaptive and defrag_scheduler flags.
